author: ReviewBombHater
quote:
After all the reviews, and deep research, I had to play it for myself. I asked my cousin to gameshare and loaded it up on my Series X.

At first, it was fine, a few ups and down due to the capped frame rate, but what can I expect? At first, certain things bugged me, unable to steal cars in Jason's neighborhood, kinda crazy I can't commit Grand Theft Auto in a game called GTA, but ight. The bugs and glitches kinda ruined the game, which in my opinion was hilarious. We crucified Cyberpunk 2077 for their bugs and glitches when they were released early, but a game that was in development for supposedly so long is given a pass? Then, I took a break, did some more research, and what threw me off the most? Is that Rockstar supposedly went Woke when making this game. I had hoped it wasn't true, but source after source of what I found says it is. No wonder the game felt different, not like any other GTA before. I was alright, gonna leave a decent review, then? The community. To absolutely review bomb and talk down about other games, while insulting gamers? Is sad. Gaming is about people enjoying the games the want, enjoying the games the been looking forward to. Gaming is about being honest, no blined to developers, not rude to other gamers. These are sad times when the gaming community rather be at each others throats than to actually try and be a community. I'm sorry GTA, you were enjoyable the few hours I played, but your woke and toxic community has absolutely ruined the image of this game for me.

author: ReviewBombHater
quote:
My honest review? It is a game you need to play to fully see how well this remake is. The game is stunning, absolutely beautiful. The graphics are beyond anything I could have expected. I played not only the original, but the 3DS remaster as well. Let me break it down

The story, is the same, being slightly rewritten, some scenes slightly altered from the original, but all done flawless. I had feared theh would have ruined it, but they didn't. A few things were removed from certain dialogue, but that's fine. 

The graphics, the art, all beautiful, beautifully done. It captured that feeling, that feeling of what I felt I was playing when I was a kid. I find it amazing, how vast and breathtaking the world is, especially now with extra details. Hyrule field used to feel empty, but now it has more life and wonder than it did before.

The music, as always, a blessing on the ears. I find myself sitting there, listening to certain musics in certain areas just for the enjoyment. Especially Saria's Song in the lost wood.

What I loved the most about this game? I spoke highly of it to all my siblings. The middle child saw me playing it awhile ago and he said "I need to play this", and he barely played a Nintendo game before, maybe Mario Kart, part of the original Ocarina of Time and that was it. He rarely plays games I enjoy, so that was a surprise. The youngest? I catch him coming home from school, taking my switch just to boot up OoT Remake and play through it. He keeps asking for help occasionally, but it warms my heart that the game I played, has reached a newer audience. 

Is this review based on nostalgia? Maybe, but it's also based on that I've played the game completely, I put close to 40 hours maybe, sometimes just hearing the music or playing the Ocarina, but mostly completing all I could before fighting Ganon. I got the better Bigoron Sword, all 100 Skultulas, all heart canisters and more. I have played this game as complete as I can, and I can tell you this, this game is amazing, it deserves the love and praise it gets. 

I had to create an account just to post this review cause it pains me to see all the hate being brought to it by people who haven't even played it properly, haven't given it a chance. It's a beautiful game, well written, with amazing art and gorgeous graphics, wonderful character designs, wonderful world design and much more. It is a game you need to personally experience, to fully understand. It may not be perfect to everyone, but to me? It is. I am grateful that I got to enjoy this game, one last time
